resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO)
resale_co.issued_by: Mount Laurel Township Department of Community Development (Construction / Code)
resale_co.contact_title: CCO questions and scheduling contact (named on the CCO application and checklist; no title given)
resale_co.lead_time: Fees are tiered by how early you apply: 11 or more days before closing is the lowest fee. The application must be submitted with payment before the inspection is scheduled; the office calls you to set the time.
requirements: All permits closed before approval (decks, pools, sheds, water heaters, furnace/HVAC, finished basements, electrical, plumbing, structural work)
Electric, gas and water on; panels, furnace and water heater accessible; furnace and water heater working and properly vented
Yard free of debris, high grass and hazards; roof, chimney, siding, gutters in good condition
Sidewalks, stairs, patios, walkways and driveways free of trip hazards
House numbers visible from the street, at least 4 inches high
Windows work with no broken or missing glass; entry doors have a working lockset and deadbolt; no double-key deadbolts or slide bolts
Handrail on stairs with 4 or more risers; guards where a walking surface is more than 30 inches above grade
Plumbing works with no leaks; hot and cold water; water temperature not over 120F
Bathroom has a working window or exhaust fan vented outside
Range anti-tip device where required
GFCI protection within 6 feet of sinks and at laundry sinks, garage and exterior outlets; covers on outlets, switches, junction boxes; panel cover with no open breaker spaces
Garage-to-house door solid wood, solid-core, steel or 20-minute rated; garage door opener plugged directly into an outlet (no extension cords); garage attic access fire rated (permit required)
Dryer vented outside with 4-inch rigid or semi-rigid metal duct (no plastic or foil); washer drains to approved drain
Pool barriers maintained; gates self-closing and self-latching, latch at least 54 inches high, opening away from pool
Any other health or safety hazard found by the inspector must be fixed

fees.label: Initial inspection, requested 11 or more days before closing
fees.quote: If requested eleven days prior to closing or longer, the fee for an initial inspection shall be $75.00

fees.label: Inspection requested 4 to 10 days before closing
fees.quote: If requested between four and ten days prior to closing, the fee shall be $100

fees.label: Inspection requested 3 days or less before closing
fees.quote: If requested three days or less prior to closing the fee for inspection shall be $125

fees.label: Discount: low/moderate income deed-restricted home or primary owner aged 65+
fees.quote: If the property is encumbered with a low or moderate income housing deed restriction and/ or the primary owner of the property is aged 65 or older, the fees shall be reduced by fifty percent (50%)

fees.label: Re-inspection (waived if within 30 days and all items fixed)
fees.quote: If the re-inspection occurs within thirty (30) days of the initial inspection and all items originally found deficient have been cured or corrected to the satisfaction of the Township inspector, the $25.00 re-inspection fee shall be waived.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the CCO application (Ordinance 2021-8 form) and mail it or drop it off with payment at Mount Laurel Township, Attn: Jennifer Parks, 750 Centerton Road, 2nd Floor, Mount Laurel, NJ 08054. Emailed applications are NOT accepted. Payment by cash, check or money order only. The office calls to schedule the inspection (Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 11:30 AM or 11:30 AM to 2:30 PM).

evidence.quote: REQUIREMENTS FOR CERTIFICATE OF CONTINUED OCCUPANCY (C.C.O.) For Resale of ALL Residential Homes
Mount Laurel Township CCO Application per Ordinance 2021-8
The application must be submitted with payment to schedule the inspection. We do not accept applications through email; they can be mailed in or dropped off at the Township building.
This checklist is intended to assist property owners, buyers, sellers, and real estate professionals in preparing for a Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO) inspection.
For questions and scheduling contact: Jennifer Parks | 856-234-0001 Ext. 1227 | jparks@mountlaurel.com
Please note that Township will NOT accept emailed applications.

resale_co.notes: Mount Laurel Township runs its own resale CCO inspection (separate from the fire department smoke/CO certificate). The CCO application (file dated March 2026) cites Ordinance 2021-8; the 2021 'Housing Inspection List' says it applies 'For Resale of ALL Residential Homes'. The June 2026 checklist replaces the 2021 list (the 2021 list named a different contact, Samantha Higarada). The application also says: 'The certificate of continued occupancy must be obtained within 90 days of the closing date. If the closing date is delayed, the seller may request an extension of the 90-day deadline from the Construction Code Official.' The fee tiers are counted from the day the request is made to the closing date. Township code (ecode360 MO0794) was not read. Construction Official: Robert Gates (856-234-0001 ext 1112); Housing Officer: Trish Hochreiter (856-234-0001 ext 1318), per the department page.

requirements: All smoke alarms must be less than 10 years old (Mount Laurel Township Ordinance 2021-19, Chapter 81, Section 81-24); take each alarm down and check the date on the back; replace any with no date
Each level needs an AC (hardwired) alarm or a DC 10-year sealed battery alarm, based on year built; all AC alarms must be interconnected
Pre-1975 homes: 10-year sealed battery alarm on each level including basement
CO alarm outside of, but near, all sleeping areas if the home has a fuel-burning appliance, fireplace or garage (CO alarms only in bedrooms fail)
Hardwired low-voltage fire alarm systems (alarm company) must be tested by an alarm contractor before the inspection; bring the contractor's certification
Breaker for the smoke alarms must be found and labeled before the inspector arrives; owner or agent turns it on and off
Homes with a generator, solar panels or battery storage need a permanent (not handwritten) 'CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER' type label within 18 inches of the main panel and the electric meter
House numbers: Arabic numerals at least 3 inches high, securely mounted, contrasting color, at least 30 inches above ground, visible from the street
No recalled smoke or CO alarms
Everything must be done before the inspector arrives; inspectors cannot install or repair anything

authorities.name: Mount Laurel Fire Department (Mount Laurel Fire District #1), Bureau of Fire Prevention
authorities.lead_time: Fee tiers are counted back from the inspection date: more than 10 days before the inspection date is the lowest fee. Inspections are each Wednesday, by appointment only; the appointment is made when the application and payment are made.

fees.label: Smoke/CO inspection, applied more than 10 days before the inspection date
fees.quote: $65 (more than 10 days prior to inspection date)

fees.label: Smoke/CO inspection, applied 4 to 10 days before the inspection date
fees.quote: $100 (between 10 days and 4 days prior to inspection date)

fees.label: Smoke/CO inspection, less than 4 days before the inspection date (based on availability)
fees.quote: $140 (less than 4 days to inspection date, based on availability)

fees.label: Change of ownership or occupancy without the certificate (penalty)
fees.quote: the owner will (will, shall, or may) be subject to a penalty of $500 per occurrence (N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3).

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply and pay online through the Mount Laurel Fire Department's Muniverse portal (linked from mlfd.org under Inspections / Forms, Residential Smoke Alarm Inspections), or in person at Fire Headquarters, 69 Elbo Lane, Mount Laurel (office hours Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 12 PM and 1 PM to 4 PM). Have the buyer's and seller's names, property address, settlement date and year built. Payment by exact change, check or charge. All fees are non-refundable; a missed time block or a failed inspection needs a new application and a new fee. Communication is by email.

evidence.quote: Any change of ownership or occupancy (including the storage of personal property) may not occur, prior to a successful inspection AND possession of a Smoke Alarm and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Inspection (CSACMAI) Certification (passed inspection).

If the assigned block of time is missed by the applicant or the applicants’ agent, another non-refundable application fee must be paid. I also understand if I do not pass the inspection, I must return to Fire Headquarters and pay another non-refundable application fee.
That all smoke alarms must be less than 10 years old as per Mount Laurel Township Local Ordinance 2021-19, Chapter 81, Section 81-24.
A certificate of Smoke Alarm Compliance is required at the change of ownership or occupancy for residential properties.
The Bureau of Fire Prevention conducts Certificate of Smoke Alarm Compliance inspections each Wednesday by appointment only.
pay a fee. (exact change, check or charge). Applications are accepted in person or scheduled on our website.
Fire Prevention Bill Glassman Fire Marshal
Additionally, the bureau ensures compliance with smoke alarm regulations during property transactions
Fire Official William J Glassman, Jr Phone (856) 234-6053 ... Email wglassman@mlfd.org

fire_cert.notes: The resale smoke/CO certificate is issued by the Mount Laurel Fire Department (Mount Laurel Fire District #1, a separate taxing body), not the Township. The Township CCO application and checklist both say 'Smoke Certificate required from the Fire Department' and point to mlfd.org. The mlfd.org smoke page embeds a Muniverse portal (geo.muniverse.us) that holds the current requirements and fees; that portal page loaded with curl on 2026-09-30. The live mlfd.org/faqs/ page shows a bot check to curl; its text was read with WebFetch on 2026-09-30 (same wording as quoted) and from an April 2025 Internet Archive copy (cited, original URL https://mlfd.org/faqs/, captured 2025-04-21). The current FAQ list no longer includes a fire extinguisher (the April 2025 copy still listed 'a 2A:10BC fire extinguisher installed in or within 10 feet of the kitchen'), and the current portal application does not list an extinguisher. The FAQ cites the 10-year alarm rule as Ordinance 1985-12 while the portal cites Ordinance 2021-19; both say Chapter 81, Section 81-24. Other bureau staff on the district site: Randy Johnson and Sam Damra (Fire Inspectors), Sarah Nawn (Clerical Staff, snawn@mlfd.org). General office email: info@mlfd.org. The state fire directory (survey 3/5/2026) lists William J Glassman, Jr as the (interim) fire official.

other_items.label: Open permits must be closed
other_items.detail: All required permits must be obtained and closed before CCO approval. Construction Department 856-234-9686.

other_items.label: Rental registration if the buyer will rent
other_items.detail: If the property will be a rental, it must be registered with the Township within 14 days of the closing date (Code Chapter 121).

other_items.label: Fire department smoke/CO certificate
other_items.detail: Smoke certificate required from the Fire Department; schedule at mlfd.org.
